questions.question: What was the day of the week on 15 February 2004?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Given: We need to find the day on 15 February 2004.

2004 was a leap year.

 
 

 Component
 Value
 
 
 
 

 Date
 15
 
 

 Month Code (February)
 3
 
 

 Century Code (2000s)
 6
 
 

 Year Code (04)
 4
 
 

 Leap Year Count (04 ÷ 4)
 1
 
 

Total = 15 + 3 + 6 + 4 + 1 = 29

29 ÷ 7 gives remainder 1.

Day code 1 = Sunday.

Therefore, 15 February 2004 was Sunday.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: What will be the product of the number of Tuesdays and Thursdays in the month of February in the year 2004?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Given:

2004 was a leap year, so February had 29 days.

February 1, 2004 was Sunday.

 
 

 Tuesdays
 
 
 
 

 3
 
 

 10
 
 

 17
 
 

 24
 
 

Total Tuesdays = 4

 
 

 Thursdays
 
 
 
 

 5
 
 

 12
 
 

 19
 
 

 26
 
 

Total Thursdays = 4

Calculation:

Product = Number of Tuesdays × Number of Thursdays

Product = 4 × 4 = 16

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 4".**

questions.question: In the year 1932, which of the following month had 5 Sundays?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

A month has 5 Sundays when:

A 31-day month starts on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday.

A 30-day month starts on Saturday or Sunday.

 
 

 Date
 Day
 
 
 
 

 Jan 1
 Friday
 
 

 Jan 2
 Saturday
 
 

 Jan 3
 Sunday
 
 

Sundays in January: 3, 10, 17, 24, 31

Total Sundays = 5

 
 

 Sundays
 
 
 
 

 5, 12, 19, 26
 
 

Total Sundays = 4

 
 

 Sundays
 
 
 
 

 6, 13, 20, 27
 
 

Total Sundays = 4

Thus, only January 1932 had 5 Sundays.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question:
Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1676e9e67d5c89d6161944b9a065cba0e1c949d3e847b6aa86ff13fbd88d42e6.png]
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: The second figure is formed by rotating both the inner arrow and the outer corner arrow by 90° clockwise.

The first pair:

The inner arrow pointing upward rotates to the right.

The outer corner arrow also rotates 90° clockwise, changing both its position and direction.

The second pair:

The inner arrow pointing right rotates downward.

The outer corner arrow at the top-left rotates 90° clockwise and moves to the corresponding new corner position with outward-down direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/542035845f4d4a99f359b4323efbdf06aebe71eac88cca6da2f86cada6c8aa2a.png] 

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

**(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)**

? : 734 :: 526 : 1054 :: 745 : 1492
questions.solution:
The Logic followed here is:

Logic: (First number × 2) + 2 = Second number

For, 526 : 1054

(526 × 2) + 2

= 1052 + 2

= 1054

For, 745 : 1492

(745 × 2) + 2

= 1490 + 2

= 1492

Now for ? : 734

(X × 2) + 2 = 734

X × 2 = 734 − 2

X × 2 = 732

X = 732 ÷ 2

X = 366

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3.**
